summary: The code runs and is syntactically correct with required imports, builds a small-world network, and simulates basic mask adoption under social influence, media, policy, and supply. However, it does not fully implement the specified entity model, interactions, or required metrics from the task. Several metrics are missing or misnamed, entities like Household/Workplace/PublicVenue/PolicyMaker are not modeled as required, and some parameter names diverge from the spec.

issues.description: Required entities and interactions (Household, WorkplaceSchool, PublicVenue, PolicyMaker, MediaSource as specified) are not implemented. The simulation uses numpy arrays and does not instantiate or use the Person/Household/Workplace/PublicVenue/PolicyMaker classes as per the spec.
issues.solution: Implement the specified entities as classes or structured agents and wire their interactions: households (norms, peer influence), workplaces and public venues (policy enforcement, contact hosting with contact_rate_modifier), a PolicyMaker issuing policies per schedule, MediaSource broadcasting messages, and Retailers with inventory/price dynamics. Use these in the MaskSimulation instead of unused dataclasses.

issues.description: Missing required metrics or mismatched names in results: sustained_adoption_duration_above_70, policy_noncompliance_rate, mask_availability_rate, adherence_probability_mean, adoption_inequality_gini_income, and time_to_target_adoption_70. Also, spec expects peak_adoption_rate but code returns peak_adoption.
issues.location: MaskSimulation.run() results dictionary and supporting computations
issues.solution: Add metrics: (1) sustained_adoption_duration_above_70: after first reaching 70%, count days with adoption >= 0.7; (2) policy_noncompliance_rate: 1 - policy_compliance_rate; (3) mask_availability_rate: fraction of agents with stock > 0 per day, and optionally endline value; (4) adherence_probability_mean: track per-agent adherence probability (wear_prob) among adopters (or all agents) and report mean; (5) adoption_inequality_gini_income: compute Gini of adoption across income groups (e.g., by quantiles’ adoption rates); (6) time_to_target_adoption_70: include in run results; (7) rename or also include peak_adoption_rate alias.

issues.description: The Person entity fields per spec (income, household_id, workplace_id, network_neighbors, adoption_state, adherence_probability, mask_inventory, information_sources, etc.) are not represented directly, preventing computation of some metrics (e.g., adherence_probability_mean) and interactions (household norms).
issues.location: Agent state representation and decision logic in MaskSimulation
issues.solution: Introduce explicit per-agent attributes aligned to spec: adoption_state separate from daily wearing, adherence_probability stored, mask_inventory as integer, info sources, and map these to decision functions. Track household_id and workplace_id and construct corresponding groupings.

issues.description: Retailer behavior is modeled as a single aggregate inventory pool; required behaviors (sell_masks, restock, update_price) and attributes (per-retailer inventory, supply_rate, price dynamics) are not implemented per entity.
issues.solution: Instantiate Retailer entities with inventory, supply_rate, and price; implement sell_masks, restock, and update_price (e.g., increase price as inventory tightens), and route purchases through retailers, considering affordability thresholds.

issues.description: Policy compliance vs noncompliance metric naming mismatch: code outputs policy_compliance_rate but the spec requires policy_noncompliance_rate.
issues.solution: Add policy_noncompliance_rate = 1 - policy_compliance_rate to results to match the spec.

issues.description: Household norms and peer influence by household are not implemented; only network-based social influence is used.
issues.solution: Create households with members and a household norms variable (norms_mask). Include household-level influence in attitude/wearing decisions, e.g., combine network mean with household adoption share using a weight.

issues.description: Contact dynamics at home, work/school, and community venues with contact_rate modifiers and enforcement strength are not modeled as specified.
issues.solution: Model contacts per location type using specified contact rates (home/work/community), enforce mask policies at workplaces/schools and public venues with enforcement_strength, and apply adherence during contacts.

issues.description: Parameters used diverge from the spec (e.g., restock_rate vs restock_rate_per_day, retailer_initial_inventory_per_capita, affordability_threshold_income_fraction).
issues.solution: Harmonize parameter names/usage with the spec: retailer_initial_inventory_per_capita, restock_rate, mask_price, affordability_threshold_income_fraction, policy_start_day, policy_mask_required_fraction, enforcement_strength, information_campaign_intensity, etc., and document mappings if needed.

issues.description: evaluate() returns a scalar mean for adoption_rate_over_time, whereas the spec defines it as a time series. While evaluation_metrics includes only adoption_rate_over_time in the spec, this mismatch can confuse downstream users.
issues.solution: Either rename metric in evaluate() to adoption_rate_mean or have evaluate return the full series (which may not be ideal). At minimum, document this behavior or add an alias.

issues.description: Neighbor influence computation loops over all agents daily, which can be slow at very large n.
issues.solution: Consider vectorizing neighbor averaging using adjacency matrices or sparse operations, or precompute normalized neighbor sums. For n=10,000 and k≈10 this is probably acceptable.
